Summary: Paul's shunning command: shun profane and vain babblings, for they will increase unto more ungodliness, and guard the deposit committed to you against oppositions of science falsely so called.
Commandment: But shun profane and vain babblings: for they will increase unto more ungodliness. O Timothy, keep that which is committed to thy trust, avoiding profane and vain babblings.
Application: Empty talk is not harmless noise: it spreads like gangrene (the next verse names Hymenaeus and Philetus). Guarding the deposit and shunning babble are two sides of the same stewardship.
Purpose: Scripture's own reason: 'for they will increase unto more ungodliness' (2 Timothy 2:16).
